s1.syndrome_frame: Pelvic mass with chronic abdominal pain and vaginal discharge
salient_findings: Pelvic mass extending to two fingers below the umbilicus
key_facts: 48-year-old postmenopausal woman
Gravida 2, para 2
3-month history of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge
Fluctuating lower abdominal pain
Fever
Progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years
Difficulty with defecation and voiding
Previous attempted myomectomy with severe adhesions
Elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level of 115.6 g/dL
Smooth, firm pelvic mass on rectovaginal examination
Limited mobility of the pelvic mass
Cervix could not be visualized or sondaged
Transabdominal ultrasound showed a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity
Separate homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa
Abdominal and pelvic computed tomography demonstrated a multilocular cystic mass

differentials: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor of the pelvis
Ovarian small cell carcinoma of the hypercalcemic type
Uterine tumor resembling ovarian sex cord tumor
per_call: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor of the pelvis
Ovarian small cell carcinoma of the hypercalcemic type
Uterine tumor resembling ovarian sex cord tumor

shortlist.label: Uterine fibroid with cystic degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Pelvic mass with cystic degeneration and elevated CA-125 level

shortlist.label: Infected hematometra
shortlist.why_kept: Brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fever, and pelvic mass with fluid and air on imaging

shortlist.label: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CA-125 level and pelvic mass with solid components on imaging

shortlist.label: Uterine leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth of pelvic mass and elevated CA-125 level

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multilocular cystic mass on imaging with potential for malignant transformation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fluctuating lower abdominal pain, fever, and progressive abdominal enlargement, combined with the ultrasound and CT findings of a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity and a distended uterine cavity with fluid and air, are consistent with infected hematometra. The elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level and previous attempted myomectomy with severe adhesions also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Uterine fibroid with cystic degeneration
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of attempted myomectomy, the current symptoms and imaging findings are more suggestive of an infected collection within the uterus rather than a degenerating fibroid.

rejected.label: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The imaging findings do not specifically suggest a malignant process, and the clinical presentation, while concerning for cancer, is more consistent with an infectious or obstructive process.

rejected.label: Uterine leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The imaging findings do not specifically suggest a malignant process, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with an infectious or obstructive process rather than a sarcoma.

rejected.label: Mucinous cystadenoma
rejected.why: The imaging findings and clinical presentation are not consistent with a mucinous cystadenoma, which is typically a benign ovarian tumor.
